## Conceptual correctness — fix these first

Unsound or contradictory concepts in the plan's design — the highest-priority gaps. The audit reports these but does not apply them (read-only-audit split, #85): the paired apply verb walks the correctness gaps only on a bare plan — completeness gaps below stay informational until a detail bundle exists. Address them with:

    plan-tool completeness-apply arm-clustering-cross-round-consensus   # walk + apply each correctness gap
    plan-tool reconcile-plan-walk arm-clustering-cross-round-consensus  # alternative interactive review/apply

- HIGH `[runfinding-consensus-target-flatten]`: The Risks section claims "A new field on `Recommendation`/`RunFinding` round-trips through generic `asdict` / `Recommendation(**r)` serialization automatically" — checked against the code, that is true only for `Recommendation`. `RunFinding` is never built by `asdict`/`Recommendation(**r)`; it is built field-by-field by `convergence_diagnosis.py`'s `_finding_from_recommendation`, which the module's own docstring calls a deliberate "persisted-field whitelist" and which copies `id`, `source`, `severity`, `impact`, `step_id`, `anchor`, `title`, `purity_verdict_provenance`, `redirect_present`, `domain` one at a time — nothing about it is generic. Architecture point 1 also names only one edit site ("the same parse site" in `review.py`) for both classes. Every cross-round consumer this plan builds (steps 1, 2, 4) reads `RunFinding`, not `Recommendation`, from history, so skipping `_finding_from_recommendation` leaves `audit_step_target` saving and reloading fine on `Recommendation` while staying permanently `None` on every `RunFinding` — silently failing Testing criterion (1)'s round-trip claim at that hop.
  - Fix: correct the Risks claim to say `RunFinding` needs its own explicit edit, and name `_finding_from_recommendation` (add `audit_step_target=rec.audit_step_target` to its `RunFinding(...)` construction) as a required site in Architecture point 1.
- HIGH `[arm-consensus-status-source]`: Architecture point 6 requires dropping a consensus target when "the target step's current status is done" — a live look-up against each step's status, not id membership. Step 4 is titled "Pass committed step ids to the diagnosis... from the convergence and completeness surfaces," and its own description commits only to feeding "committed step ids," matching `evaluate_arm_clustering`'s existing `declared_step_ids: Sequence[int]` parameter that Architecture point 7 says stays unchanged. Neither step 2 (which owns the new classifier function) nor step 4 (which supplies the plan data) says where the per-step status value the point-6 check needs actually comes from — a bare id list carries no status — and this is exactly the round-3 `stale-done-step-target` gap this plan already fixed once, now left without a stated data source.
  - Fix: state in step 4 that the plan data threaded from `cmd_convergence`/completeness surfaces into the classifier carries each committed step's current status alongside its id (e.g. the `Step` objects themselves or an id→status map), not a bare `Sequence[int]`.
- MEDIUM `[convergence-diagnosis-leaf-import-claim]`: Step 5's acceptance criterion says CLAUDE.md's `convergence_diagnosis.py` import line and the module's own "cycle-free leaf" docstring paragraph "name the same fact today" — checked against the code, they already don't. CLAUDE.md says the module "imports only `review_persistence`, `review`, `locator`, `convergence`"; the module's own docstring says "it imports `review_persistence`, `review`, and `locator`... so every import sits at module top" — the docstring already drops `convergence`, and both already drop `granularity` (`from plan_tool.granularity import GRANULARITY_SPLIT_SOURCE`). If step 5 only appends the new `audit_shapes` edge step 2 adds, both statements ship still wrong about `granularity` and still disagreeing with each other about `convergence` — the exact staleness step 5 says it wants to prevent for the next session.
  - Fix: have step 5 correct both statements to the module's full current import set (`review_persistence`, `review`, `locator`, `convergence`, `granularity`, plus the new `audit_shapes` edge), not only append the one edge this plan adds.

## Conceptual completeness — reported, not auto-applied

Coverage gaps in the plan's own ideas are reported for visibility in this bare-plan audit. Apply actions for this axis are withheld until a complete detail bundle exists, so these findings are informational for now.

- MEDIUM `[matches-tier1-false-consensus]`: The Risks section covers misattribution only when `_matches` is bypassed ("if `_matches` is bypassed instead of reused"); it never covers the same failure when `_matches` is used exactly as specified. `_matches`'s tier 1 ("step focus") matches two findings purely on a leading `step<N>`/`step-<N>` token parsed out of `anchor` (`c_focus == r_focus`), with no additional check that the anchors or titles agree. Plan-audit findings always carry `step_id=None`, so two genuinely different findings that both happen to be anchored `step5-...` in different rounds would match at tier 1, letting the newer one inherit an unrelated older finding's `audit_step_target` as if it were the same finding recurring — fabricating the two-round recurrence evidence this plan exists to require, for a finding that is really new this round.
  - Fix: add this as a named risk distinct from the bypass case already listed, and add a testing case with two differently-worded findings sharing a leading step token across two rounds, asserting they are never treated as one recurring finding for consensus.
- MEDIUM `[arm-clustering-evidence-omitted]`: Architecture point 7 lists exactly three arguments to pass into `evaluate_arm_clustering` unchanged — `consensus_targets`, `material_finding_ids`, `declared_step_ids` — and never mentions `material_finding_evidence`, the fourth input the same-execution caller always builds from each finding's real `anchor`/`source`. Left unset, the leaf still returns a well-formed advisory (it fills in a placeholder empty-anchor/empty-source entry per id when none is passed), but every cross-round advisory would render blank anchor/source instead of the finding's actual ones, unlike the same-execution advisory.
  - Fix: have step 2 also build `material_finding_evidence` from each matched `RunFinding`'s `anchor`/`source`, the same shape the same-execution caller already builds from `Recommendation`.
